unit_result_entry.title: Generalized limits retain Jensen convexity, mean-motion bounds, zero-frequency bounds, and value distributions
unit_result_entry.why_material: Theorems 1 and 2 assert that uniform convergence in an inner ordinary strip plus mean convergence on a half-strip yields a uniform Jensen limit, convexity, motion and zero-frequency inequalities, convergence of approximating Jensen functions, and convergence of asymptotic value distributions.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: These theorems are the transfer layer later instantiated with partial Euler products.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Half-strip Besicovitch-type mean convergence replaces uniform moving-interval means
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: To treat zeta below the ordinary almost-periodic region, the source replaces two-sided uniform interval means by fixed-origin half-line means and defines analytic convergence in mean with arbitrary positive index on reduced half-strips.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Nested rectangles turn mean approximation into local analytic control
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The proof localizes half-strip convergence using nested rectangles: mean convergence controls local sup differences, local maxima have mean values and sublinear growth, and ordinary almost periodicity supplies a uniform nonvanishing point in each window.
